primary_diagnosis_treated: Metabolic syndrome (including hypertension, obesity, prediabetes, dyslipidaemia, iron‑deficiency anaemia, chronic sinusitis)
nice_guideline_used: NICE CG181 / PH46 / NG28 / NG136 / NG107 / NG203

medications.purpose: Control hypertension while avoiding overtreatment (BP 96/57 mmHg); already prescribed, dose reduced
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive; dose reduction appropriate for hypotension

medications.purpose: Stop to reduce hypotension and adverse metabolic effects; thiazides not first‑line in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 advises against high‑dose thiazides in metabolic syndrome and recommends stopping when causing hypotension

medications.purpose: Primary cardiovascular disease prevention in metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 recommends a statin for QRISK ≥10 % or any metabolic‑syndrome component

medications.dose: 500 mg orally once daily with evening meal, titrate to 500 mg twice daily as tolerated
medications.purpose: Improve glycaemic control in high‑risk prediabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 recommends metformin for high‑risk pre‑diabetes when lifestyle alone is insufficient

medications.dose: 0.25 mg subcutaneous weekly, titrate to 1 mg weekly as tolerated
medications.purpose: Weight management in obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) and additional glycaemic benefit
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 supports GLP‑1 RA for obesity when weight loss is a priority

medications.purpose: Treat iron‑deficiency anaemia pending confirmation of iron studies
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG107/NG203 advise iron replacement when ferritin <200 µg/L or TSAT <20 %

medications.dose: 50 µg per spray, 2 puffs each nostril once daily
medications.nice_justification: NICE guidance for chronic sinusitis recommends intranasal corticosteroid for symptomatic relief

medications.duration: Lifelong – review at 5 years or if symptoms change
medications.purpose: Contraception and reduction of menstrual blood loss
medications.nice_justification: Standard contraceptive device; no contraindication in metabolic syndrome

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive hypotensive effect leading to symptomatic low BP
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue hydrochlorothiazide; monitor blood pressure after lisinopril dose reduction

interactions_checked.interaction: No clinically significant interaction; additive glycaemic benefit
Iron may reduce absorption of levonorgestrel if taken together
interactions_checked.action: Separate dosing by at least 2 hours

contraindications.reason: eGFR unknown; NICE NG28 contraindicates metformin if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² due to lactic acidosis risk
contraindications.alternative: Confirm eGFR >30 before initiating; if <30, use lifestyle measures or DPP‑4 inhibitor

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated in patients with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN‑2 (NICE GLP‑1 RA guidance)
contraindications.alternative: If such history exists, consider orlistat or other weight‑loss options

contraindications.reason: Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevation of transaminases would contraindicate initiation (NICE statin monitoring)
contraindications.alternative: Obtain baseline LFTs; if abnormal, defer statin or use lower dose after investigation

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed >30 mL/min/1.73 m² for ACE‑I dosing and metformin initiation; serum creatinine/eGFR must be obtained before starting metformin.
Baseline liver function tests not available – required before initiating atorvastatin and for ongoing monitoring.
Lipid profile and QRISK score not available – needed to confirm statin indication per NICE CG181.
Serum potassium level not provided – monitor after ACE‑I dose change to detect hyperkalaemia.
Allergy status unknown – verify no allergy to ACE‑I, statin, or metformin before prescribing.
treatment_summary: The plan reduces antihypertensive overtreatment by stopping hydrochlorothiazide and lowering lisinopril, initiates a statin for primary CVD prevention, adds metformin (pending eGFR) and a GLP‑1 RA for prediabetes and obesity, treats presumed iron‑deficiency anaemia, and provides intranasal steroids for chronic sinusitis. All choices follow NICE CG181, NG136, NG28, NG107/NG203, with monitoring for renal function, liver enzymes, lipid response, glycaemic control, iron status, and blood pressure.
